title: sessions listing shows 0 messages, no timestamps and no titles: claude_code discover() never reads transcripts
description:
**Observed on real data (read-only run against `--home` default, origin/develop `9fc6584`):** `botspy sessions` prints `MSGS 0`, `LAST ACTIVITY —`, `TITLE —` and empty `metadata` for **every** claude_code row; `-o json` shows `started_at`: "", `last_activity_at`: "", `message_count`: 0, `metadata`: {} for all 61 listed sessions. The same sessions open fine: `botspy show 00fcdc4d` reports "3 messages, started 2026-09-22T10:41:27.032Z".

**Repro:**
1. `cargo build --release` at origin/develop; run `./target/release/botspy sessions --limit 5` (real home) → every row `0  —  —`.
2. `./target/release/botspy sessions --limit 5 -o json` → all `message_count` 0, timestamps empty.
3. `./target/release/botspy show 00fcdc4d` → same session shows 3 messages with timestamps. Inconsistent.

**Expected:** the listing carries real per-session data — message count, first/last activity timestamps, and title — consistent with `botspy show` for the same id, without writing anything to the source.

**Suspected code:** `ClaudeCodeSource::discover()` in `src/adapters/claude_code.rs` (~line 81-106): it pushes `SessionSummary { id, agent, project_id, ..SessionSummary::default() }` per `.jsonl` file name and never reads the transcript. `extract()` in the same file already parses everything correctly.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- `discover()` populates `started_at`, `last_activity_at`, `message_count` and title metadata per transcript, matching what `open()`/`show` reports for the same id.
- Regression test with a **synthetic fixture** (temp-dir transcript or the committed `tests/fixtures` corpus — never real transcripts): a transcript with N timestamped records must list `message_count: N` and the correct first/last timestamps in `discover()` output.
- `botspy sessions` and `botspy show` agree on message counts and timestamps for the fixture sessions.
- Read-only guarantee unchanged: no writes into the source tree.
- Note: `botspy sources`, `botspy doctor` and `botspy show` already work correctly on real data; only the listing path is broken.
- Related: the local-store ingestion epic BOTSPY-6f173d builds on `Adapter::discover()` (task BOTSPY-a48fb1) — populated summaries benefit it, and it changes no adapter code, so no conflict.
